sessionName: one session, ninety-five minutes, mostly waiting

ops.title: Oven on, three trays out
ops.body: 220 °C fan while you load, dropping to 200 °C once the trays go in. Line all three with paper. Drain and dry the chickpeas on a tea towel now — they will not crisp wet.

ops.title: Trays in — chicken, chickpeas, peppers
ops.body: TRAY A: 600 g chicken breast, salt, garlic powder, onion powder. Nothing else. 25 min. TRAY B: 250 g drained chickpeas, 1 tbsp rapeseed oil, 2 tsp jerk seasoning (5 g). 35 min, shaken twice. TRAY C: 160 g red pepper and 70 g red onion in wedges, 1 tsp rapeseed oil. 25 min.

ops.title: Pan 1 — the bolognese (longest job, start it early)
ops.body: 90 g onion, 135 g carrot and 330 g courgette, all grated, into rapeseed oil on medium for 6 min. 120 g turkey mince in, broken up and browned properly — 5 min, don't rush it. 400 g passata, oregano, a bay leaf, salt. Lid ajar, lowest heat, 30 min.

ops.title: Pan 2 — chipotle beef
ops.body: 165 g 5% beef mince browned hard in a dry pan. 2 chopped chipotles in adobo (30 g), 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 100 ml water. 10 min until it's thick and glossy.

ops.title: Pan 3 — efo riro base (no spinach)
ops.body: Blend 160 g red pepper with 90 g red onion. Into 1 tbsp rapeseed oil on medium-high and cook down 8 min until it darkens and thickens. 220 g passata, 10 min. Then 27 g egusi slaked with a little water, stirred in, 5 min until it thickens and goes grainy. Stop there — the spinach belongs at the plate on Wednesday, not here.

ops.title: Eggs on
ops.body: 5 medium eggs into boiling water for 8 minutes, then straight into cold. Peel them now while they're easy. Three are for Tuesday's snack (1 her + 2 him); the other two will get eaten.

ops.title: Chicken and peppers out
ops.body: Chicken rested 5 min, then sliced or left whole — whole keeps better. Peppers and onion into their own box. Chickpeas stay in until 0:45.

ops.title: Pan 2 free — plain rice on
ops.body: 320 g brown rice, dry, cooked plain. 25 min. This covers Monday's lunch, Tuesday's lunch and Tuesday's dinner.

ops.title: Chickpeas out — jar, lid OFF
ops.body: They should rattle on the tray. Into a jar, uncovered, on the counter. Sealed in a box they go soft by Tuesday.

ops.title: Pan 3 free — the jollof
ops.body: 95 g brown rice, dry, cooked in a blended base of pepper, tomato, onion and a little stock until the liquid is gone. 25 min. Keep it slightly under — it gets a second heating on Wednesday.

ops.title: Rice the cauliflower — the big job
ops.body: Two heads, about 1.4 kg once florets are riced in a food processor (pulse, don't run it — you want couscous, not paste). Store it RAW. It cooks in three minutes at the plate and holds far better uncooked.

ops.title: Shred for two slaws — and Friday's salmon slaw
ops.body: 515 g red cabbage and 230 g carrot, shredded fine, into one box with a piece of kitchen paper on top to take the moisture. Thursday's burger slaw, Friday's wrap AND Friday's salmon slaw all come out of this.

ops.title: The two jars
ops.body: WHITE SAUCE: 115 g Greek yoghurt, 1 grated garlic clove, lemon juice, salt, and far more black pepper than feels reasonable. Shake. SUYA: mix your own — 3 parts ground roasted peanut, 1 part chilli, then ginger, garlic powder and stock powder to taste (12 g total covers Tuesday's snack).

ops.title: Bolognese and rice off — cool them FAST
ops.body: Spread the rice out on a cold tray in a thin layer. Both into the fridge within the hour. This is the one genuine food-safety point of the day: rice left to cool slowly at room temperature is the classic way to make yourself ill.

ops.title: Portion and label
ops.body: Everything into boxes marked with the day it's for. Five minutes now saves the Wednesday evening argument about what the orange one is.

D0-019: 3 whole eggs (150 g: 1 her/50 g + 2 him/100 g) go to Tuesday's snack — a clean whole-egg split that replaces the original fractional '1½ eggs' figure. 2 spare eggs get eaten separately.

D0-014: corrected from the original 335 g/two-consumer figure — Friday's salmon slaw (a-d5d, 180 g cabbage) was omitted from the original op text. 185+150+180=515 g exactly, matching provisioning's need figure. Carrot stays 230 g (a-d5d uses no carrot from this batch).
Seasoning weighing (PLAN §4): the original op gave a mix ratio only, no batch gram figure. 12 g is grounded to a-d2s's actual consumption (5 g her + 7 g him) rather than an arbitrary jar size.

midweek.heading: Tuesday night
midweek.body: Move Wednesday's fish and prawns from the freezer to the fridge. If you're buying them fresh instead, buy them Wednesday — not before.

midweek.heading: Wednesday
midweek.body: Ten minutes. Salad and any fruit topped up. Thursday's steak out of the freezer if it's in there. Check the chickpeas still rattle; if not, 4 minutes in a hot dry pan on Wednesday evening.

midweek.heading: Thursday night
midweek.body: Friday's salmon from the freezer to the fridge.

D0-003 substitution applied to prose throughout (chickpea/pepper trays, bolognese pan, efo riro base pan) — all Sunday cooking oil hits a hot pan or hot oven, so it's named 'rapeseed oil' in the op text. None of these Sunday-only cooking oils carry a gram figure in the source (volume measures only — tbsp/tsp) and none map to a per-cover covers entry in any consuming meal, so no new gram figures are invented here (rule 9); only the word is substituted.

'minutes' per op is the elapsed time until the next op begins (from the original clock stamps), i.e. the hands-on window before attention moves elsewhere — not the full background cook time already stated inline in each op's own body text (e.g. the chicken tray's 25 min, the bolognese's 30 min simmer).
